---
title: Marfa's architecture
description: The parts of Marfa, from the instance that holds a person's data to the programs that reach it, and which of them your program is.
job: A builder learns the parts of Marfa and which one their program is.
kind: concept
---

Marfa has one center, the **instance**, which holds everything its owner keeps: files first, then notes, tasks, bookmarks and what other services send. **Every other part is a program outside the instance** that reaches it through its HTTP API, with a credential.

## The instance

An instance is one running Marfa server and the data it keeps, in one SQLite database and a folder of files. It belongs to one person, its **owner**. [Install Marfa](/run/install) shows how to run one.

**The instance is the source of truth.** Programs read from it and write to it, and never talk to each other. When two of them change the same thing, the instance decides the outcome ([Versions](/build/versions)), and every copy comes into line with it.

## What it holds

Everything is an **item**: one file, photo, note, bookmark or conversation. Its **type** says which properties it holds, and Marfa checks every write against it ([Items and types](/build/items-and-types)). Around an item sit:

- **Tags and extensions:** free labels, and an app's own data kept on the item ([Properties and metadata](/build/properties-and-metadata)).
- **Tables:** rows in typed columns, such as a conversation's messages ([Tables](/build/tables)).
- **Edges:** typed links to other items, such as a photo attached to a note ([Edges](/build/edges)).
- **A file's bytes,** kept once as a **blob**, however many items name them ([Files](/build/files)).

Every change is an **event** in one log, which a program follows to stay current ([Events and webhooks](/build/events)).

## Who can reach it

Nothing reads or writes an instance without a **credential**, and a credential reaches only what it was given: these types, read or edit, and these powers. A script or a connector holds a **key**. An app or an agent signs in with OAuth, so the owner sees what it asks for and approves it ([Access](/build/access)).

## Which part is your program

What sits between a program and the API decides what it can do:

- **The Swift SDK and the CLI** embed the **core**, a Rust engine that sends their requests and can keep a **working copy** of the items they need. A program with a working copy is a **device**: it reads offline and sends its writes when it reaches the instance ([Working copies](/build/working-copies)). A [synced folder](/use/sync-a-folder) is a device whose working copy is a folder of ordinary files.
- **The TypeScript SDK** sends each request straight to the API and keeps no copy. Web pages and scripts use it.
- **An agent,** such as Claude or Codex, connects to the instance's MCP server or runs the CLI ([Connect your agent](/connect-your-agent)). **MCP does what the API lets the same credential do,** no more.
- **A connector** is a program the owner runs that brings in records from another service, such as GitHub or a calendar ([Connectors](/build/connectors)).

<WhatReachesIt />

Apps made by WithMarfa reach the instance the same way, through the same API and credentials as anything you build.
